title: Struct with a Struct
story: You're building an address book app. A Person has a name, but they also have a home address — which itself has a street and city. How do you model this nested data?
why: Real-world data is nested — structs inside structs let you model it directly.
analogy: A Person contains an Address like an envelope contains a mailing label — the label is a distinct thing attached to the envelope.
try_it: Add a `work: Address` field to Person. Create someone with both a home and work address, then write a function that returns the full address as a single string.
tips: Define inner structs BEFORE the outer struct that uses them — the compiler reads top to bottom
Use dot notation to drill down: `person.home.city` reads left to right
You can create nested structs inline instead of using a separate variable for the inner value
common_mistakes: Forgetting to define the inner struct before using it as a field type in the outer struct
Using commas instead of semicolons between struct fields
